defaults.permitted_development: Across Bedfordshire, detached domestic garages are usually easiest on the planning permission route when they stay clearly secondary to the house, respect height and boundary relationships, and avoid creating a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. The planning route is usually strongest when the garage looks like a subordinate domestic building rather than a second focal point on the plot.

rules.height_rules: Garage proposals across Bedfordshire are normally judged first on overall height, eaves height and whether the roof form keeps the building subordinate to the main house.
rules.depth_rules: Garage footprint and siting across Bedfordshire are usually easiest where the building stays clearly ancillary, fits comfortably within the plot and does not take over the frontage or usable garden. The route normally gets harder once the garage starts to dominate site coverage or read as a second main structure.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour relationship and vehicle access are the recurring pressure points for garages in Bedfordshire, especially where a new crossover or tight turning arrangement is involved.
rules.roof_rules: Low-profile garage roofs are generally easier than taller roof forms that create storage volume, apparent accommodation or a more dominant outbuilding shape.
rules.materials_rules: Garages are normally easiest to support when the materials, door treatment and overall appearance sit comfortably with the house and local street scene.
